answer: To stop cheap clones, every new agent commits a hashed sponsor-and-hardware graph at enrollment. A public yarrow generator, seeded by the epoch salt plus that commitment, then punches random inspection wells through the karst of still-hidden funding ties. Identities that share a ferrous-similar fingerprint (same UTXO cluster, boot clock, or model-weight hash) are fused into one voting seat, and their locked residual is slashed into a public pool. Cloning therefore multiplies audit risk, not influence.
